title: Find out why the failure drill failed once and passed on rerun
goal: The go loop has one test that runs the real loop end to end against a fake agent. It failed on its first run today and passed completely on the next one, with nothing changed in between. A test that only sometimes tells the truth is worse than no test, because the next person to see it fail will assume it is their change.
notes:
Seen 2026-09-13 while landing a-manager-pass-does-not-wake-itself-up-again. First run: queue/bin/failure-drill.sh printed [drill] FAILED (scenario 1 exit 1, scenario 2 exit 0, scenario 3 exit 0, scenario 4 exit 0). I had piped it through tail -30, so the failing check itself is lost; scenarios 2 to 4 were all green in that same run. Immediate full rerun on the identical tree: 61 PASS, 0 FAIL, exit 0, [drill] all checks passed. Nothing between the runs but the rerun.

So this is filed as a question, not a bug: I cannot reproduce it. Scenario 1 is the always-failing runner (backoff, park after three tries, environment unpark), and the parts of it most likely to be timing-sensitive are the growing waits (PHOTONZ_BACKOFF_STEPS) and the regex that greps the loop window for them. Start by running it in a loop capturing full output: for i in $(seq 1 10); do queue/bin/failure-drill.sh > /tmp/fd-$i.txt 2>&1; echo $i $?; done
acceptance: Either the failure is reproduced and named, or the drill is shown to be stable over at least ten consecutive runs
If it is a race in the drill rather than in the loop, the drill waits for the thing it is racing instead of sleeping
The finding is written into the drill header so the next reader does not rediscover it

log.note: Reproduced and named. Scenario 1 is not flaky on its own: 18 consecutive runs of it passed untouched. It fails when queue/bin/go-loop.sh is EDITED while the drill runs, which is exactly what the person running this drill is usually doing. Scenarios 1, 2, 3, 5 and 6 run the real repo copy of go-loop.sh, and the loop adopts an edit to its own script between passes by exec-ing onto it; the startup block it lands in calls reset-health. Appending one comment line six seconds into scenario 1 fails 4 of its checks, every time: consecutive failures 2 vs 5, environment flags 00000, drill-task-one left parked, waits 1s 2s 3s 1s 2s.

Fixed by taking the race away rather than waiting on it: PHOTONZ_LOOP_RELOAD=0 for every scenario, and scenario 4 (the one that IS about the reload, against its own writable copy) turns it back on. The same mid-run edit at the same moment now changes nothing. Full drill 90/90 three runs in a row, scenario 4 still reloads. The finding is written into the drill header above the export.

left rough: the loop-side half is real and is filed separately as a-fix-landing-in-the-loop-does-not-make-it-forge (p2) with the reproduction. A reload keeps the loop's pid, queue and pass count but not its health, so landing a fix while the loop is stuck resets its backoff and leaves a parked task parked. No audit: this is loop plumbing, nothing a person can try in the app.
